gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-adlam: Noto Sans Adlam keeps its curve endings well apart. Line after line, its tall, full c, s and z keep the text open and unhurried, a quiet foil to Origami.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-imperial: Noto Sans Imperial Aramaic reads approachably, its c holding both ends apart like open pincers beneath the unshaded strokes of Origami. Down a full page it stays easygoing and unfussy.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-khojki: Modern and clean, Noto Sans Khojki leaves its exits wide enough to pass light through, against the fat crossbars of Origami. Paragraph after paragraph, each large-eyed e stays clear.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-lisu: Monoline swagger up top, tidy lettering below. Origami is best at loud, poured-lead lowercase, while Noto Sans Lisu handles quiet duty with generously curved s shapes and tiny ascender gaps.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-saira: Glass-tube lettering with a hollow core. Shrink Origami and that hollow tube look would fade, whereas Saira, a sans-serif, keeps a visible gap in each s and rounded letters reaching high.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-sarpanch: Heavy, cord-like curves lead the way. Beneath Origami, Sarpanch brings a clearly open-mouthed e and a compact gap above the x-height, so whole paragraphs of it read approachable and unhurried.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-sen: Sen reads tall and tidy, each lowercase letter traced in a line of constant weight. And its curves stop before turning inward, a modest foil to the poured-lead lowercase of Origami.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-sulphur-point: Marker-pen steadiness runs top to bottom here. Origami and Sulphur Point both hold a constant, marker-like line, and that shared single stroke is what ties their different builds together.
gen-dafont-outrun-future-gf-noto-sans-ca: Noto Sans Carian reads crisp and open, its terminals apart like scissor blades. Across a full page it stays clean and level, a restrained partner for the wide-spaced, outlined letters of Outrun Future.
gen-dafont-outrun-future-gf-noto-sans-ol: Outrun Future draws wide-set letters as constant-width outlines you could trace with a finger, their ascenders kept short. Noto Sans Old Sogdian stays crisp and wide-mouthed as the text runs on.
